title: December, 2008
logline: Does Chloe come home. A postcard — a real one, handwritten — from Portland. She's moved. Portland is three hours. She doesn't come.

panels.composition: The mailbox. A postcard. A bridge. Handwriting — hers, the tiny capitals, back. WOOD reading it in the alley.

image.prompt: a young man reading a handwritten postcard of a city bridge at a mailbox in a gravel alley, a small dog, December, muddy watercolor

panels.composition: The card: 'W — Portland. Three hours from you, which is the closest I've been in nine years and the farthest, somehow. Julian's here. Not for Christmas. Neither am I. The firm. — C.' The handwriting is back. The strip draws every letter.

image.prompt: a panel that is the back of a postcard in tiny cramped handwritten capitals, drawn with evident relief at the return of handwriting
image.notes: Letter after. The handwriting returns. Julian, second mention.

balloons.text: Three hours. She's three hours away and she wrote it down instead of driving it.

image.prompt: a young man holding a postcard and talking to a dog with a complicated face

panels.composition: The corkboard. The card pinned writing-out, like the 2001 one. Two cards now that show their words. The rest, photo-out.

image.prompt: a crowded corkboard where a young man pins a postcard with its handwritten side facing out beside one other card pinned the same way, all the others photo-side out, no words

art.palette: limited; Sundays in watercolor, good now
art.paper: bristol; the browser; from 2008 coastal newsprint a week behind

notes: Portland. Three hours. The handwriting back. The second card pinned writing-out.
